The present Application is fled invoking inherent powers of this Court as provided under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seeking directions for quashing of C.R. No. 271 of 2017, registered at the behest of the Respondent No. 2 for offence punishable under Section 376 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The Respondent No. 2 (Original Complainant) herein has fled C.R. No. 271 of 2017, with the R.A.K. Marg Police Station, Mumbai, on 09.12.2017.

It is alleged by the Respondent No. 2 that, after being divorced in 2009, she had registered her name on the matrimonial website, at the instance of her R.V.Patil 2/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt parents in February 2012.
Upon being registered on the said matrimonial website, she had received interest from various persons with different profles.
The present Applicant who was also registered on the said matrimonial site was approached by the Respondent No. 2, as she was interested in his profle.
Thereafter, she came to Mumbai on 22.12.2012.
When the Applicant was informed about her arrival, they met each other.

After meeting Nandamitra Vinayak Pawar vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65377010/
1 personally, they started chatting with each other.

sentences.text: 3. It is stated in the FIR by the Respondent No. 2, that she had been to Mumbai for the treatment of cancer in October 2013.
When she was taking treatment in Mumbai, the Applicant used to meet her.
During her frequent visits, friendly relations developed between the Respondent No. 2 and the Applicant.

It is alleged by the Respondent No. 2 that, on 15.05.2016 when she had been again in Mumbai for her medical examination, the Applicant visited the guest house where she was staying and he forcibly imposed intimacy on her.
While doing so, the Applicant informed the Respondent No. 2 that, he was going to get divorce very soon, thereafter he would marry her.
Relying on his assurance, she had physical relationship with the Applicant.

4. The Respondent No. 2 further alleged that after being intimate with the Applicant on 15.05.2017,
the very next day i.e. on 16.05.2017, she again went out with the Applicant and spent time with him,
they had lunch, snapped photographs and had a good time.
After that, the Applicant had stopped having contact with the Respondent No. 2.

At last, when she R.V.Patil 3/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt called him in June 2016, on his cellphone and inquired as to when he was going to decide about their marriage, the Applicant informed her that, she should not expect much from him and he merely likes to spent time with her.

In spite of various calls and messages, the Applicant did not respond to her and ultimately she received a call from one unknown lady informing her, that the Applicant had married somebody else without being divorced from his frst wife on 30.05.2016.
On this background, the Respondent No.2 has fled the FIR alleging offence under Sections 376 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

5. The Applicant has fled the present Application wherein it is the categorical stand of the Applicant,
that when he met the Respondent No. 2 he had informed her about the pendency of his matrimonial dispute before the Thane Court.
He had asked her to go ahead with her life as the matrimonial dispute did not seem to be ending in near future.
He had also given moral support to the Respondent No. 2 during her visit for treatment of Cancer at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai.
According to the Applicant, whenever she used to visit Mumbai, she was always accompanied by someone with her.

6. It is contended by the Applicant that he suddenly received a notice issued by the Respondent No.
1 informing that the Respondent No. 2 has lodged a complaint against him and he was directed to remain present for inquiry within a period of two days.
When he visited the concerned police station he came to know about the details of the complaint fled against him.
He has totally denied that, he had any sexual R.V.Patil 4/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt intercourse with the Respondent No. 2.
The Applicant further categorically states that, no such incident had ever taken place.
He had merely friendly relations with the Respondent No.2.
It is contended by the Applicant that, the said complaint has been fled only with malafde intention to harass the Applicant.

Even the bare perusal of the FIR discloses that the Respondent No. 2 had friendly relations with the Applicant and no such incident of sexual intercourse had ever taken place.
7.
We have heard the learned counsel for the Applicant as well as the learned APP for the State.

sentences.text: We have gone through the copy of the FIR annexed to the Application, the Respondent No. 2 has alleged that the Applicant has committed offence of rape and cheating which is made punishable under Section 376 and 420 of the IPC.
According to the Respondent No. 2, the present Applicant has promised to marry her and subsequently he has refused to marry her.
He has also forced himself on the Respondent No. 2 and had sexual relations with her once on 15.05.2016.
The Respondent No. 2 had acceded to his overtures because the Applicant had promised to marry her.

According to the Respondent No. 2, while forcing himself upon her, he had promised to marry her, therefore his subsequent conduct of refusing to marry her amounts to cheating and act of forcibly establishing sexual relations with her amounts to rape.

8. On going through the statement of the Respondent No. 2 which is recorded on 30.11.2017, it is apparent, that the R.V.Patil 5/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt Respondent No. 2 and the Applicant have been introduced on matrimonial platform in December 2012.
After that, they have also personally met each other at Mumbai.
After meeting each other personally, though the Respondent No. 2 was residing at Nagpur and the Applicant was residing at Mumbai, they were constantly in touch with each other through telephone.
The Respondent No. 2 in the meanwhile suffered Cancer and she was visiting Mumbai for a treatment from 16.10.2013.
During her treatment whenever she had come to Mumbai, they spent time together.
The Respondent No. 2 has mentioned that she and the Applicant were in love with each other.
She was aware that the Applicant was not divorced till then.
She constantly in touch with the Applicant.
Even her son was accompanying her when she met the Applicant on many occasions as stated by the Respondent No. 2 herself.

From 2012 to 2016, the Respondent No. 2 and the Applicant had met various occasions, however, she did not mentioned that the Applicant ever tried to force himself on her or established sexual relations with her, prior to 2016.

9. In her statement she has stated that, it was only on 15.05.2016 when she had been to Mumbai and was staying in the guest house of the Oriental Insurance Company, while her son was also present outside the room, the Applicant has forced himself on her and while doing so, he had again assured her that they would soon marry, as he is likely to get divorced.

From the narration of the contents of the FIR it it is undisputed position which emerges is that from October 2012 to May 2016 the Respondent No. 2 was aware that the matrimonial proceedings of the Applicant for divorce were R.V.Patil 6/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt pending and he has never forced himself on her or tried to establish sexual relations with her, till then.
In fact, their relations were friendly and they have spent lot of time with each other, whenever the Respondent No. 2 used to visit Mumbai.

10. It does not seem probable, that the incident as stated by the Applicant could have taken place when her son was accompanying her and very much present outside the room, where the said incident is stated to have taken place.
The conduct of the Applicant on the very next day i.e. on 16.05.2017 also does not auger-well with her allegations.
She alleges that, the Applicant has imposed himself on her on the previous day and it was against her will.

If at all it was against her will, her normal conduct should not have been to accompany and spend time with the Applicant visiting the hotels and other places and having photographs with him till 11 o'clock at the night.
It also needs to be considered that the present FIR has been fled on 30.11.2017 against the Applicant, for the incident which has taken place on 15.05.2016.

If at all the Respondent No. 2 would have been Nandamitra Vinayak Pawar vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65377010/
3 aggrieved by the behaviour of the Applicant, she would have immediately fled complaint to the police authorities very next day or within reasonable time, but she has not done it.

sentences.text: She has fled the present complaint belatedly after more than a year and half.
11. The Respondent No. 2 has fled the complaint for the offences punishable under Section 376 and 420 of the IPC.

As far as the allegation of the Applicant regarding rape is concerned, the case of the Applicant does not fall under any of R.V.Patil 7/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt the seven circumstances mentioned in the defnition of rape.
The said sexual act was neither against her will nor without her consent and nor any of the rest of fve circumstances mentioned in the defnition of rape.
In fact, in the FIR she mentions, that no sooner the Applicant has alleged to have closed the door of the room.

She has inquired with him as to when they would be getting married, to which according to her, he responded by stating that he is likely to get divorce very soon and he would be required to marry soon since he was nearing his ffties.

The Respondent No. 2 has not mentioned that she has shown any kind of resistance to him or she has refused to have sexual relations with him, therefore, the said act as mentioned by the Respondent No. 2 does not fall within the defnition of rape.
The other Section which has been invoked is Section 420 of the IPC provides for punishment for cheating.

As far as the defnition of cheating is concerned, there is an element of deceit in cheating as Section 415, which reads as under:
"415. Cheating- Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to "cheat".
12.
In the present case, the contents of the FIR nowhere indicate that the Applicant had ever promised to marry the Respondent No. 2.

In fact, since the beginning it was very R.V.Patil 8/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt much clear that the divorce proceedings of the Applicant were pending, therefore,
unless the divorce proceedings could come to an end, he was not legally free to marry anybody.
Though the Respondent No. 2 was well aware about it and she continued her friendship with the Applicant.
There is no element to deceit in the present case.
13. The Hon'ble Apex Court had an occasion to deal with a case of Section 375 of the IPC, wherein the issue regarding woman engaging in sexual relations on false promise of marriage was considered.

The Apex Court in case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar V/s. State of Maharashtra and Anr.
1 and in particular para- 16 has observed, as under:
16.

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar V/s. State of Maharashtra and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the promise to marry is false and the intention of the maker at the time of making the promise itself was not to abide by it but to deceive the woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a "misconception of fact" that vitiates the woman's "consent".
On the other hand, a breach of a promise cannot be said to be a false promise.

To establish a false promise, the maker of the promise should have had Nandamitra Vinayak Pawar vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65377010/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: no intention of upholding his word at the time of giving it.
The "consent" of a woman under Section 375 is vitiated on the ground of a "misconception of fact" where such misconception was the basis for her choosing to engage in the said act.

In Deepak Gulati this Court observed: (SCC pp.682-82, paras 21 &
24) "21. ...
There is a distinction between the mere breach of a promise, and not fulflling a false promise.

Thus, the court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused; and whether the consent involved was given after wholly understanding the nature and consequences of sexual indulgence.
There may be a case where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused, and not solely on account of 1 (2019) 9 SCC 608.

R.V.Patil 9/10 22 APL.307.2018.odt misrepresentation made to her by the accused, or where an accused on account of circumstances which he could not have foreseen, or which were beyond his control, was unable to marry her, despite having every intention to do so
. Such cases must be treated differently.

24. Hence, it is evident that there must be adequate evidence to show that at the relevant time i.e. at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever, of keeping his promise to marry the victim.
There may, of course, be circumstances, when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.
The "failure to keep a promise made with respect to a future uncertain date, due to reasons that are not very clear from the evidence available, does not always amount to misconception of fact.
In order to come within the meaning of the term "misconception of fact", the fact must have an immediate relevance".

Section 90 IPC cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning,
the accused had never really intended to marry her."

Therefore, in view of the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred matter,
we do not fnd that there is a case made out for proceeding with the prosecution against the Applicant.
14. The present Application has been fled by the Applicant for quashing of the FIR invoking the powers of this Court as provided under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

Though it is a settled position of law, that the Court should be guarded in use of its extra ordinary jurisdiction vested in it by law,
while quashing FIR or criminal proceedings, however the Court can certainly exercise the inherent powers to secure the ends of justice and to prevent the abuse of process of law.

sentences.text: In the present case, we have gone through the FIR and in our opinion, prima facie there is no any offence or a case made out against the Applicant.
The allegations in the FIR do not disclose any cognizable offence justifying an investigation by the police authority or and full-fedged trial.
If the said proceedings are allowed to be continued, it would amount to abuse of process of law.

16. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that this is a ft case, where this Court should exercise its jurisdiction to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court, so as to secure the ends of justice.
In our view, the analysis made by us above would squarely fall within the guidelines laid down in the case of State of Hariyana V/s. Bhajan Lal2

entities.text: State of Hariyana V/s. Bhajan Lal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the allegations set out in the complaint, we do not fnd that it constitutes offence of which cognizance has to be taken, justifying any investigation by the police authorities under Section 156(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Hence, in view of the observations made hereinabove, the FIR No. 271 of 2017 registered with R.A.K. Marg Police Station, Mumbai, against the Applicant is hereby quashed and set aside.
No order as to costs.
